items.stem: What best describes an ITIL 4 'value stream'?

options.text: A series of steps an organisation uses to create and deliver products and services to a consumer
options.rationale: Correct: a value stream is a combination of activities an organisation performs to deliver value to a consumer.

options.text: A single ITIL practice executed end to end
options.rationale: A value stream draws on several practices; it is not one practice.

options.text: A fixed hierarchy of management approvals
options.rationale: A value stream is about the flow of work to value, not an approval hierarchy.

options.text: A catalogue of all services offered
options.rationale: That is closer to a service catalogue, not a value stream.

items.explanation: Correct: a value stream is a combination of activities an organisation performs to deliver value to a consumer.

items.stem: A recurring issue has caused several incidents. Which practice is primarily responsible for finding and removing its underlying cause?

options.rationale: Correct: problem management identifies causes of incidents and manages workarounds and known errors.
Incident management restores service quickly; it does not focus on root-cause removal.
Change enablement controls changes; it may implement a fix but does not diagnose the cause.
The service desk is the point of contact; it logs and coordinates but does not own cause analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: problem management identifies causes of incidents and manages workarounds and known errors.
